title: Keep only the positives
hints: Start from `double_all`: the same `match` with a `[]` case and an `x :: rest` case. The empty list still gives `[]`.
In the `x :: rest` case there are two answers. When `x > 0`, put `x` in front of `keep_positive rest`. Otherwise the answer is `keep_positive rest` alone.
`| x :: rest -> if x > 0 then x :: keep_positive rest else keep_positive rest`

answer.code:
let rec keep_positive l =
  match l with
  | [] -> []
  | x :: rest -> if x > 0 then x :: keep_positive rest else keep_positive rest
answer.explain: The empty list keeps nothing, so it gives `[]`. For `x :: rest`, the function first finds the positives of `rest`. It puts `x` in front of them when `x > 0` and leaves `x` out otherwise. 0 is not positive, so it is left out.
